title: National, prospective, controlled and randomized, open-label, multicenter, non-inferiority study on the benefit of low-dose pulsed ultrasound (LPUS) for the treatment of upper and lower extremity non-union compared to surgical intervention
summary:
Background:
Fracture non-unions or commonly described, as false joint formation is a bone fracture that has not healed after at least 6 months.
The standard treatment for non-unions is surgery. The disadvantages of surgery are the need for a further stay in hospital and possible complications from the surgery.
An alternative to surgery is treatment with low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS). The ultrasound signal stimulates bone healing via biological reactions at cellular level. The advantage of this pain-free method is that it is non-invasive and carries no risks. LIPUS treatment has been used for many years with good results. The treatment of non-unions with LIPUS is therefore considered to have the potential to be an alternative treatment to surgical intervention. However, the benefits compared to surgical intervention have not yet been proven in a trial.

Objective:
The aim of this study is to demonstrate that treatment with low-intensity pulsed ultrasound is not inferior to surgery in patients with fracture non-unions.

Design:
The trial will be conducted in Germany at approximately 20 sites. The trial will include 370 patients of at least 18 years with non-unions and a bony defect ≤ 1 cm. Patients with an unstable osteosynthesis and patients with non-unions older than 24 months are not allowed to participate.

The main objectives (primary endpoint) are fracture healing and functional recovery of the affected limb.
Further endpoints are quality of life, functional complaints, and activities of daily living, duration until fracture healing and until full weight-bearing is achieved. In addition, complications of all kinds will be collected.

The patients at home carry out treatment with LIPUS (intervention group) independently for 20 minutes a day. The duration of treatment should be 200 days in total. The surgery (control group) is carried out according to the currently valid standards.

LIPUS treatment is assumed to be non-inferior to surgical treatment if the proportion of fracture healings 12 months after the start of treatment is less than 25% lower in absolute terms in the LIPUS treatment group than in the surgical treatment group.

interventions.name: intervention group: daily treatment with low-intensity pulsed ultrasound for 200 days, at minimum 180 days (compliance 90%)
control group: surgery of the non-union in accordance with the guidelines

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- non-union of the upper or lower extremity including clavicle
- fracture > 6 months and < 24 months
- primary osteosynthesis of the fracture
- bony defect < 1 cm
- closed soft tissue
- signed informed consent
- health insurance by law
Exclusion criteria:
- instability of the non-union
- non-union of the spine or the cranium
- non-union of the small bones of the hand or the toes
- non-union after osteotomy
- long spiral fractures
- pathological fractures due to maligne tumors or metastases
- operation within the last 4 months
- infection/osteomyelitis of the non-union, defects of soft tissue
- therapy with cytostatic drugs
- pacemaker
- pregnancy/breast feeding
- comorbidity, which influences the compliance
- participation in another interventional study
